questions.title: When to show 'Welcome back'
questions.context: Returning players see a small 'Welcome back, name' text on screen right after joining. If you reconnect often, it can feel like noise.

options.label: Only after 6+ hours away
options.detail: The text shows only if you were gone 6 hours or more, so quick reconnects stay quiet.

options.label: Every time you join
options.detail: Same as today: the text shows on every single join, even 2 minutes after a crash.

options.label: Never
options.detail: No welcome-back text. New players still get the full welcome.

questions.title: Where to say 'Be kind, /rules'
questions.context: New players get one grey line about chat logging 45 seconds after joining. We want players to see the rules once without adding more chat spam on the first screen.

options.label: Add it to the grey line
options.detail: That one line becomes: chat is logged for 30 days, be kind, /rules, plus the Privacy link. No extra line.

options.label: Own line in the welcome
options.detail: A short 'Be kind. /rules' line appears together with the welcome, next to 'Next: follow the flames'.

options.label: No extra line
options.detail: Rules stay one click away in /menu and /help. Nothing added to the first minute.

questions.title: Where the 'hide players' switch lives
questions.context: With 300 players at spawn, some people want to hide everyone else to keep the game smooth. You asked for a quick toggle at spawn. The main menu stays clean, so it will not get a button for this.

options.label: Toggle in /settings and the You menu
options.detail: One click flips Everyone and Nobody. Nothing new on the main menu, in your hotbar or as a command.

options.label: Hotbar item at spawn
options.detail: A dye item in your hotbar, only in the spawn world, flips it with one click. Adds one new item to look after.

options.label: Skip until spawn lags
options.detail: Build nothing now. We add it only when 300 players at spawn actually cause lag.

questions.title: What a joiner gets in their Starter pack
questions.context: When a new player joins a friend's island, they get their own small pack in the inventory, so nobody has to share the chest. The tutorial asks them to plant 3 wheat, so they need seeds.

options.label: Tools, food and seeds
options.detail: Missing starter tools, 16 bread, 8 wheat seeds and 8 bone meal. The tutorial's farming step works on any island.

options.label: Tools and food only
options.detail: Missing starter tools and 16 bread, as built today. Seeds must come from the friend's island.

options.label: Almost the whole chest
options.detail: Missing tools, bread, seeds, bone meal, 2 saplings, a crafting table and a chest. Only the lava bucket is left out.

questions.title: Timer on the Forge 'Starter kit' button
questions.context: If a starter tool goes missing, the Forge 'Starter kit' button gives back only the tools you lack. Today you can use it once every 24 hours per profile.

options.label: No timer
options.detail: Use it any time, only missing tools are given. Staff get an alert if one profile gets more than 20 tools in a day.

options.label: Keep the 24 hour timer
options.detail: Same button, but only once a day per profile, as it works today.

questions.title: Chests on Frost Peak and Ash Dunes
questions.context: Later there will be three starter islands: Ember Meadow, Frost Peak and Ash Dunes. Should their starter chests differ?

options.label: Same kit everywhere
options.detail: Same tools, seeds and food on all three. The island build and the first view give the flavour. Easiest to balance.

options.label: One flavour stack each
options.detail: Same kit plus one small extra stack that fits the theme, for example spruce saplings on Frost Peak.

options.label: Fully different chests
options.detail: Each island has its own item list and its own guide page. Most work, and each one must be balanced.

questions.title: Starter tool after the first Forge upgrade
questions.context: Starter tools cannot be sold, traded or put on the auction house. Today, upgrading one to tier 2 at the Forge turns it into a normal tool that can be sold. That would let new profiles turn free tools into money.

options.label: Stays bound forever
options.detail: The tool stays yours for the whole season, however far you upgrade it. Free tools can never become money. Reverses the old plan.

options.label: Becomes a normal tool
options.detail: As built: the first tier-up costs money and then the tool can be sold or traded like any other.
